narrative_purpose: The chapter's representative image: an ordinary piece of Pandoran crust treated as a specimen, which is exactly how the chapter treats it - the end of a thirteen-billion-year supply chain, sitting on a bench.
subject: A single fist-sized chunk of dark rock resting on a bare metal field bench. The rock has been cut clean through on one side, and the flat cut face is turned toward the viewer: dark grey-green stone shot through with tiny bright metallic flecks that catch the light. The uncut sides are rough and dull. Nothing else sits on the bench.
scene: A field-station workbench at night, open to the outside. Behind and far above the bench, out of focus, the vast banded curve of a gas giant fills the upper part of the sky, dim and hazy. A few faintly glowing plants at the edge of the frame throw a soft cyan light across the bench surface.
camera: Close three-quarter view, slightly above the rock, shallow depth of field so the rock's cut face is sharp and the sky behind dissolves into haze.
light: One warm amber field lamp low from the left, raking across the cut face so the metallic flecks glint; cool cyan fill from the glowing plants at the right edge; deep indigo shadow everywhere else.
palette: Void-indigo background, deep teal-indigo stone, scarce warm amber lamp light on the cut face, tiny bright metallic glints, a cool cyan rim from the plants.
style: Painterly naturalist specimen plate, hand-observed, soft edges, visible brush texture.
detail_level: High on the cut face - individual mineral grains and metallic flecks readable; low and hazy everywhere else.
composition: The rock sits just right of centre, filling roughly a third of the frame. The bench runs out of frame to the left as dark negative space. The upper third is dim hazy sky.
consistency_notes: The gas giant behind is Polyphemus - cream and rust banding, kept dim and out of focus so it never competes with the rock. The rock is ordinary basalt-like crust, not glowing or exotic.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no watermark, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no glowing minerals, no unobtanium, no floating rock
